answer: A reputation graph makes sybil attacks expensive: every agent is a vertex, and trust flows only along edges earned by real, costly work. A new identity starts with no incoming edges, so even a swarm of fresh vertices carries no weight. Like a zephyr bending a plume of smoke, cheap identities drift apart under scrutiny because they cannot fake the history of verified transactions that anchors real agents. Attackers must therefore pay the full cost of building genuine reputation for each identity, which destroys the economics of mass fakery.
